messages:
Priya K: handing off evening shift — I'm primary until 02:00 UTC. Miguel L is secondary. Quick status: we’ve seen an uptick in p99 token latency for model-pool-us-east across some long-context requests. No full customer outages, but a few 502s from the infer-proxy last hour. Incident-bot posted an alert earlier: kvcache-thrash (see below).

Priya K: coverage gaps — I’ll be offline for 25 mins at 00:45 UTC for a hard pause. Miguel, can you cover the pager window 00:45–01:10 if anything bubbles? If not, we fallback to oncall escalation (Sam H).

Miguel L: ack, I can patch that window. If it looks like KV eviction, I’ll try the lightweight fix first (drain + restart) before full rollout.

Priya K: runbook links — adding quick pointers:
- KV cache emergency play: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
- Infer backend restart steps: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infer-backend-restart
- Customer-impact script + severity table: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/impact-assess

Priya K: quick mitigation checklist (copy/paste):
```
# check nodes under memory pressure
kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -h

# drain noisy runtime pods (graceful)
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60

# restart infer backend on a single pod for canary
kubectl rollout restart deployment/infer-backend -n inference --selector=zone=us-east --timeout=120s

# toggle fallback routing (control plane -- internal tool)
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --pool=model-pool-us-east --to=small-model-variant
```

Priya K: logs example we saw (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T23:18:05Z] infer-proxy ERROR: downstream 502 from infer-backend-7fdc, conn-reset
[2026-03-14T23:19:01Z] infer-backend INFO: kvcache evict 1.2G, active_keys=120k, miss_rate=0.23
[2026-03-14T23:20:12Z] autoscaler WARN: burst queue depth 54, scaling delayed by 12s
```

Jun W: note — before restart, please run the KV probe to avoid noisy restarts. Small script: 
```
curl -s https://metrics.internal/kvprobe?pool=model-pool-us-east | jq .active_keys,.eviction_rate
```
If eviction_rate > 0.15, prioritize draining clients and enable prefix caching.

Miguel L: on the routing fallback — I’ll enable small-model-variant as temporary for 10m while we stabilize. That should reduce token cost too so ops doesn’t freak out :grimacing:.

Sam H: FYI for escalation policy — if latency>p99 2x baseline for >10m AND 10% of requests returning 5xx, escalate to ENG-SRE pager (pager duty) and inform CS. Use template in runbook "impact-assess" to fill customer-facing blurb quickly.

Priya K: tagging followups: @Miguel L please paste the rollout-id after you toggle fallback. @Sam H I'll DM the exact customer list if we start seeing 5xx.

incident-bot: ALERT summary: 4820011200 — kvcache-thrash detected on model-pool-us-east. Pages sent to oncall at 23:19 UTC. Current status: degraded (no active mitigations). Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4820011200

Miguel L: fallback enabled (rollout-id: rollout/20260314-3807). Toggling for 10m now. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood/boards/pools/model-pool-us-east

Priya K: monitoring quick checks:
- p99 latency: dashboard > latency > p99 window = 18s -> target < 6s
- 5xx rate: logs > http > 5xx = 0.6% -> watch for >1%

Jun W: left a quick remediation snippet in the runbook: if eviction cycle is cyclical, bump KV max-entries by 15% on the pod spec and trigger rolling restart (small batch). Link included in runbook.

Sam H: thanks all — I’ll be reachable if this escalates. Miguel, if you need cover for longer than 01:10, ping the oncall rota (/@oncall) and mark as handover in the bridge notes. :thumbsup:

Miguel L: will do. marking as primary takeover if needed.

Priya K: wrapping — I’ll check back at 01:05 UTC for status update. Leaving this thread as the quick log for the handoff.

Miguel L: ack, see you.
